resources.string: Resolve IPv4 / IPv6 and address types
Resolve one host and identify private, loopback and link-local address types. No port scan.
Choose a tool. Get facts and a next step.
Up to 16 ports; timeout vs refusal
Explicit small subnet, up to 64 addresses
Send a magic packet to a chosen address
Extract IP and MAC from text
Combine DNS, Ping and TCP checks
Enter parameters and start. No probes run automatically.
Checking… You can stop at any time.
Review internal addresses and sensitive details first. Nothing is uploaded automatically.
No matching tool. Try Ping, DNS or subnet.
Check only networks you own or are authorized to inspect. Target: %1$s\nPorts: %2$s\nUp to 64 addresses and 4 TCP ports. No reply does not prove a device is absent.
Send a magic packet to %1$s.\nMAC: %2$s\nOnly use for authorized devices. A sent packet does not prove the device woke up.
Check parameters: timeout 1–15 seconds, count 1–20. Follow the target and option hints.
The check did not complete. Review the target, connection and system capabilities.
Phone restrictions do not imply switch restrictions. Verify the connected device and vendor, then run the appropriate command manually. This is a preview only.
Command preview accepts only a plain hostname or IP.
Send bounded ICMP probes. No reply may be a firewall policy, not an outage.
Rootless first. Unsupported capabilities are reported instead of displaying permission errors as route results.
Requires a supported no-fragment option. No response does not prove a smaller MTU.
Examples: A or AAAA @1.1.1.1. A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, NS, TXT, SOA and PTR are supported.
Single target, up to 16 ports. Example: 22,80,443 or 8000-8003. Authorized targets only.
Enter a complete http:// or https:// URL. No account, password or request body is sent.
Enter hostname and TLS port (usually 443). Validation failures are never ignored.
Shows current network data exposed by Android. Gateway or Wi-Fi details may be unavailable.
Enter a private IPv4 subnet such as 192.168.1.0/26. Up to 64 addresses and 4 TCP ports; no automatic subnet scan.
Target: broadcast address or device IPv4. Option: MAC. Wake-on-LAN must already be enabled on the device.
Enter a MAC such as 00:11:22:33:44:55. The offline vendor list is limited; unknown vendors are not guessed.
Offline reference, not a scan. A common port purpose does not identify a running service.
Paste log or configuration text. Addresses are extracted offline; no AI upload is needed.
Run basic checks against one target. Enter one TCP port; default 443.
The report will fill an AI draft. Review and send it yourself; only then is it sent to your selected provider.
